Resting on the east coast of the Peloponnese near Porto Heli, Amanzoe is a modern-day Acropolis from which 360-degree views encompass olive groves and the Aegean sea. Pavilions and villas all offer private pools with stunning views and fragrant gardens, whilst speedboats await at the beach to zip between nearby islands. Role We are seeking an experienced and accomplished Director of Finance who embodies Aman’s commitment to excellence, integrity and financial leadership to join Amanzoe, in the Peloponnese, Greece. Reporting to the General Manager, the Director of Finance plays a pivotal role in overseeing the property's financial operations, driving financial performance and ensuring effective financial planning, reporting and internal controls. This senior leadership position requires a strategic and hands-on approach, strong commercial awareness and the ability to provide financial guidance that supports the resort's operational excellence and long-term success. Responsibilities Lead and oversee all financial operations of Amanzoe, ensuring accurate financial reporting, compliance and effective internal controls. Act as a strategic financial partner to the General Manager and Executive Committee, providing financial analysis, recommendations and guidance to support business decisions. Direct the annual budgeting, forecasting and financial planning processes, including operational expenditure and capital investments. Monitor financial performance, identify opportunities for revenue optimisation and cost efficiency, and implement strategies to achieve financial objectives. Oversee monthly financial statements, balance sheet reconciliations, cash flow management and financial performance reviews. Ensure compliance with Greek taxation requirements, accounting regulations, statutory reporting obligations and applicable financial policies. Maintain effective financial controls over inventories, purchasing, contracts, cash management and the property's assets. Review commercial agreements, supplier contracts, insurance arrangements and financial commitments to protect the property's interests. Lead, mentor and develop the Finance team, promoting accountability, professional development and succession planning. Collaborate with department leaders to strengthen financial awareness, optimise resources and support the resort's operational and service standards. Requirements Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration or a related field. A recognised professional accounting qualification or membership, such as CPA, ACCA or equivalent. Minimum ten years of relevant experience in finance within a five-star hotel or luxury hospitality environment, including experience in a financial leadership role. Comprehensive knowledge of financial management, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting and internal controls. Strong understanding of Greek taxation legislation, statutory reporting requirements and applicable accounting standards. Knowledge of the Uniform System of Accounts for the Lodging Industry (USALI). Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications; experience with SunSystems is an advantage. Demonstrated experience in leading Finance teams, supporting business decisions and managing financial performance. Excellent analytical, organisational, leadership and communication skills, with proficiency in written and verbal English. You must have the legal right to live and work in Greece. Benefits At Aman Group, we believe that our colleagues are at the core of our success. We offer a range of benefits to support both your personal and professional growth across existing and upcoming destinations. From exciting development opportunities to competitive compensation, we prioritise and support your career journey, making you feel valued, included and at home. Access to professional development and leadership learning resources, including eCornell Single Accommodation Private health insurance coverage. Fuel allowance. Discount on Food and Beverage outlets and Aman Retail boutique. Employee Wellness Program including complimentary Yoga, Tennis and Gym classes. Amanzoe Elite Program with discounts at various restaurants and local stores. Participation in colleague events and property celebrations. Provided meals and coffee breaks while on duty. Additional benefits in accordance with the property's senior management benefits policy. If you thrive in an ultra-luxury environment and are passionate about excellence, leadership and contributing to the success of an exceptional property, we invite you to apply to join us on our journey.

review_candidates.title: Data Protection Officer
review_candidates.description: Data Protection Officer | FCA-Regulated FinTech (Foreign Exchange and International Payments) F-11, Islamabad | Permanent | Full-time | Office-based preferred; hybrid or remote considered Safeguard the personal and financial data of private and corporate clients for an FCA-regulated FinTech that has been moving money across borders for 23 years. Aetheria Group is recruiting a Data Protection Officer on behalf of a closely affiliated international FinTech: an established foreign exchange and international payments business headquartered in London, with offices in Cyprus and in F-11, Islamabad. This is a senior, permanent appointment with statutory independence and direct access to senior leadership, for a professional who wants to own and build a data protection function rather than administer one. About the organisation For 23 years our client has provided currency exchange, international payments, forward and option contracts and multi-currency accounts to private clients, including people buying property abroad, relocating overseas or moving significant sums internationally, and to corporate clients managing currency risk. It is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority as both a payment institution and an investment firm, handles more than £1 billion of client payments a year, and pairs modern payment technology with dedicated portfolio managers. Why this role matters Every client relationship involves bank account details, identity and address documents, source-of-funds evidence, payment instructions, recorded calls and the results of anti-money-laundering, sanctions and fraud checks. That data is commercially valuable, attractive to criminals and closely scrutinised by regulators. As the business expands its digital channels and adopts automation and AI, it needs a Data Protection Officer who keeps that data lawful, secure and proportionate, and who gives leadership the confidence to grow on firm foundations. The role You will be the organisation’s designated Data Protection Officer: informing and advising the business, monitoring compliance and reporting to the highest level of management, with the independence the law requires. You will work closely with the Chief Executive, Managing Director, Compliance and the MLRO, Operations, Technology and Marketing, and act as the contact point for the UK regulator, the Information Commission’s Office (ICO), and for clients and colleagues exercising their rights. What you will do Governance and accountability Lead compliance with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, and PECR, and advise on EU GDPR as it applies to the Cyprus operations. Maintain the records of processing, lawful-basis assessments, retention schedule and accountability evidence across onboarding, dealing, payments, marketing and HR. Advise on and monitor Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for new products, platforms, outsourcing, automation and AI. Rights, complaints and breaches Run subject access requests, other rights requests and data protection complaints end to end, with a documented MLRO review step so that no response prejudices a suspicious activity report or investigation. Lead personal data breach response: triage, risk assessment, 72-hour ICO notification decisions and client communications, aligned with operational-incident reporting to the FCA. Financial crime and client protection Advise Compliance and the MLRO on the data protection dimension of customer due diligence, sanctions and PEP screening, adverse-media checks, transaction monitoring and record retention under the Money Laundering Regulations. Govern the handling of criminal-offence and special-category data, including information recorded about clients in vulnerable circumstances under the FCA’s Consumer Duty, and call-recording and communications retention. Marketing, technology and suppliers Set the rules for compliant private-client and corporate marketing: consent, legitimate interests, the soft opt-in, cookies, and outbound email and telephone activity, now that PECR fines match UK GDPR levels. Assure processors and partners, including payment and banking partners and identity-verification, CRM, cloud and telephony providers, through due diligence, contracts and periodic review. Govern international transfers between the UK, the EU and Pakistan, and support information security governance on access control, encryption, logging and payment-card data. Culture and reporting Deliver practical, role-specific training to dealers, portfolio managers, operations and marketing colleagues across all three offices. Report to leadership through a quarterly data protection assurance dashboard covering risk, rights requests, breaches, DPIAs, supplier assurance and regulatory change. What you will bring Substantial, demonstrable experience applying UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, or EU GDPR, in practice. A background as a DPO or as a privacy, information governance, compliance or risk professional. Experience handling sensitive data at scale, whether special-category, criminal-offence or financial. Proven handling of subject access requests and personal data breaches, including regulator-notification decisions. DPIA experience, or strong demonstrable knowledge. A sound grasp of controller and processor relationships, data processing agreements and supplier due diligence. Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to turn complex law into clear, decisive advice and to challenge senior stakeholders constructively. High integrity, discretion and independence of judgement. Desirable Experience in financial services, payments, foreign exchange, e-money, banking or FinTech, ideally in an FCA-regulated firm. An understanding of how anti-money-laundering obligations, the tipping-off offence and data subject rights interact. Familiarity with the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 reforms, including recognised legitimate interests, automated decision-making and the new complaints requirement. PECR and digital marketing compliance, including cookies, marketing automation and outbound campaigns. UK and EU experience, and international transfer mechanisms such as the IDTA, the UK Addendum and EU Standard Contractual Clauses. AI governance, including DPIAs for AI tools and automated decision-making. Information security frameworks such as ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials or PCI DSS. A recognised certification such as CIPP/E, CIPM or the BCS Practitioner Certificate in Data Protection, a legal qualification, or a prior DPO appointment. These are desirable, not essential. We will support the right person to deepen this knowledge through structured mentoring from senior UK data protection and compliance expertise. Working pattern and location Permanent, full-time, Monday to Friday. 08:30–17:30 UK time, moving with UK daylight saving: 13:30–22:30 PKT while the UK is on Greenwich Mean Time (late October to late March) and 12:30–21:30 PKT during British Summer Time. Based at our F-11 office in Islamabad. We prefer office-based working; for an exceptional candidate we will consider hybrid or remote arrangements. Close, daily collaboration with colleagues in London and Cyprus. What we offer A competitive, negotiable salary that reflects your experience. Paid annual leave, and paid sick and casual leave for unplanned absence. Registration in the EOBI pension scheme, with employer contributions. A senior, board-visible role with genuine statutory independence. Structured mentoring, professional development and a long-term career path. Real international exposure across the UK, Cyprus and Pakistan. A state-of-the-art, modern office in F-11 with excellent facilities. A 20% staff discount on all food and drink at Rove, Islamabad’s largest rooftop restaurant and lounge, in our office building. Regular staff social events. Our workplace We have built a modern, welcoming workplace where people are treated with respect, good ideas are heard whatever their source, and colleagues from different backgrounds work as one team across three countries. We invest in our people, value sound professional judgement and expect everyone to act with integrity. How to apply Apply through LinkedIn with your CV. You do not need to include your photograph, date of birth, marital status, CNIC number or home address. We do not use this information to assess applications. Selection includes a first interview, face to face at our F-11 office or by video for candidates outside Islamabad, and an online interview with senior leadership, both conducted in English. We will share the client’s name with shortlisted candidates. We review applications as they arrive and may close the advert early once we have a strong shortlist. Equal opportunities We are committed to equal opportunities and to recruiting on merit against the genuine requirements of the role. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, sex, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy or maternity, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. If you need any adjustment to the application or interview process, please tell us and we will make reasonable arrangements. We take a zero-tolerance approach to harassment, bullying and discrimination. Pre-employment checks Any offer is subject to satisfactory pre-employment screening appropriate to a regulated financial services role, including references and verification of identity, qualifications and employment history. Your application data Aetheria Group will use the information you provide only to recruit for this role. It will be handled confidentially and shared only with those involved in the hiring decision, including the client’s leadership if you are shortlisted. Retention is governed by our recruitment privacy notice, available on request, and you may ask how your data is handled at any time.

You will play a crucial role in ensuring that the company's accounting and financial processes meet established standards, promoting accurate financial reporting and effective control. This is your chance to contribute to the success of a growing organization by supporting our finance department and advance your career in a collaborative and innovative environment. Key Responsibilities Review monthly bookkeeping activities and support month-end and year-end closing processes. Prepare and review financial statements and management reports. Ensure the accuracy of financial data, including general ledger, trial balance, and balance sheet reconciliations. Review accounting transactions, journal entries, and intercompany balances. Liaise with external auditors and support statutory audit processes. Monitor and support ERP system operations and accounting controls. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. 5-7 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably within a multinational environment. Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting, and closing procedures. Advanced Excel skills and experience with ERP/accounting systems. Experience with Oracle NetSuite ERP is highly desirable. Excellent command of English, both written and spoken. Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills with a high level of attention to detail. Benefits We believe in rewarding talent and dedication. Here's what you can expect as part of our team: Competitive full-time salary; Private Health Coverage on the Company's group program; Flexible Working Hours; Top-of-the-Line Tools; Professional Development: Benefit from language courses, specialized training, and continuous learning opportunities; Career Growth: Work with some of the most innovative and exciting specialists in the industry; Dynamic Work Environment: Thrive in a setting that offers challenging goals, autonomy, and mentoring, fostering both personal and company growth. If you want an exciting challenge, work with some of the coolest technologies, and enjoy your time doing it, then join us! Submit your detailed CV in English, quoting reference: ( FC/11/26 ). You may also consider all our other open vacancies by visiting the career section of our website (www.eurodyn.com) and follow us on Twitter (@EURODYN_Careers) and LinkedIn. EUROPEAN DYNAMICS (ED) (www.eurodyn.com) is a leading European Software, Information, and Communication Technologies company, operating internationally (Athens, Brussels, Luxembourg, Copenhagen, Berlin, Stockholm, London, Nicosia, Valetta, Vienna, Den Haag, Hong Kong, etc.) The company employs over 1100 engineers, IT experts, and consultants (around 3% PhD, 41% MSc, and 54% BSc). We design and develop software applications using integrated, state-of-the-art technology. Our current IT projects have a value exceeding 300 million EURO. EUROPEAN DYNAMICS is a renowned supplier of IT services to European Union Institutions, international organizations, European Agencies, and national government Administrations in 40 countries and 4 continents. As part of our dedication to the diversity of our workforce, we are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity without regard for race, colour, national origin, ethnicity, gender, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or religion. review_candidates.title: Assistant CRA
review_candidates.description: Work Schedule Standard (Mon-Fri) Environmental Conditions Office Join Us as an Assistant Clinical Research Associate – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation! We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years. As part of our global team, you’ll have the opportunity to perform remote activities on assigned projects in liaison with the CRA and study Clinical Lead. As an Assistant Clinical Research Associate, you'll provide support with site preparedness, logistical support to the monitoring process, and assist with assigned tasks for site management and remote monitoring in accordance with SOPs and regulatory guidelines. You may be assigned limited site contact activities during study start-up, site management, recruitment, and close-out phases. What You’ll Do: Completes study and site management activities as defined in task matrix, and as applicable and directed for study assigned. Completes and documents study-specific training. Orients and trains on any study-specific systems. Provides in-house support during pre-study assessments and with pre-study assessment waivers, as agreed for project. Supports to customize Site ICF with site contact details, as needed. Performs remote review of EMR/EHR checklist and supports collection, as applicable assessments. Verifies document collection and RCR submission status; updates site EDL and verifies site information. Reviews patient facing materials and review translations, as directed. Supports site staff with the vendor related qualification process, where applicable. Provides support by ensuring system access is requested/granted and revoked for relevant site staff during pre-activation and subsequent course of the study. Provides support to follow-up on site staff training, as applicable. Coordinates and supports logistics for IM attendance, as directed. Supports maintenance of vendor trackers, as directed. Coordinates study/site supply management during pre-activation and subsequentcourse of the study. Supports Essential Document collection, review and updating in systems, as applicable. Follows up and supports on missing study vendor data like ECGs, lab samples, and e-diaries, as directed. Supports ongoing remote review of centralized monitoring tools, as directed. Supports Site payments processes by coordinating with various functional departments within organization and site. Supports system updates and reconciliations, as directed and follows-up on site invoices throughout the study period. Performs reconciliaton tasks on assigned trials including but not limited to CRF and query status, deviations, SAEs and safety reports, as applicable. Verifies document collection status in company systems and drives action for missing/incomplete/expired documents and open document findings, as directed. May perform other assigned site management tasks, as directed by CRA and as per Task Matrix. Maintains & completes administrative tasks such as expense reports and timesheets in a timely manner. Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor's degree in a life science discipline Previous experience that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job (comparable to 1 - 2 years). In some cases an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Basic medical/therapeutic area knowledge and understanding of medical terminology Ability to attain and maintain a working knowledge of ICH GCP, applicable regulations and company procedural documents Effective oral and written communication skills Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills Good organizational and time management skills and strong attention to detail, with proven ability to handle multiple tasks efficiently and effectively Proven flexibility and adaptability Ability to work in a team or independently, as required Well-developed critical thinking skills, including but not limited to critical mindset, in-depth investigation for appropriate root cause analysis and problem solving Proficient computer skills with good knowledge of MS Office ability to learn and use appropriate software. Leverage modern technology when applicable Ability to extract pertinent information from all study documents, electronic study data systems, CTMS and dashboards Excellent English and Turkish language and grammar skills The Assistant CRA role does not involve regular travel, however, any direct, promotional opportunities in the CRA career track will require frequent travel (60-80%). Why Join Us? When you join Thermo Fisher Scientific, you become part of a global team that values passion, innovation, and a commitment to scientific excellence. You’ll work in an environment where collaboration and development are part of the everyday experience - and where your contributions truly make a difference. What we offer: As well as being rewarded a competitive salary, we have an extensive benefits package based around the health and well-being of our employees. We have a flexible working culture, where PPD® clinical research services truly value a work-life balance. We’ve grown sustainably year on year but continue to offer a collaborative environment, with teams of colleagues eager to share expertise and have fun together. We are a global organization but with a local feel. Our Mission is to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. As one team of 100,000+ colleagues, we share a common set of values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - working together to accelerate research, solve complex scientific challenges, drive technological innovation and support patients in need. #StartYourStory with PPD, part of Thermo Fisher Scientific, where diverse experiences, backgrounds and perspectives are valued. Our 4i Values: Integrity – Innovation – Intensity – Involvement If you resonate with our 4i values above, and ultimately wish to accelerate the delivery of safe and effective therapeutics for some of the world’s most urgent health needs, submit your application – we’d love to hear from you! Apply today to help us deliver tomorrow’s breakthrough.

review_candidates.title: Analyste d'Exploitation AS400 (H/F)
review_candidates.description: À propos de nous SEA TPI accompagne les plus grandes entreprises dans la mise en œuvre de Centres de Services IT innovants, couvrant 100% du Run des productions informatiques. Fondée il y a plus de 30 ans, SEA TPI a su rapidement s'imposer comme un acteur de référence sur le marché par son approche pragmatique associant savoir-faire technologique et réponse à des attentes métier. Mission Dans le cadre du renforcement de notre dispositif d’exploitation, nous recherchons un Analyste d’Exploitation IBM i confirmé (H/F) justifiant de plus de 5 ans d’expérience dans la gestion d’environnements de production critiques. Au sein d’une équipe de production composée de trois personnes, vous participerez au maintien en conditions opérationnelles des plateformes IBM i ainsi qu’à l’exploitation des flux et des traitements associés. Vous évoluerez dans un environnement exigeant en matière de disponibilité et contribuerez activement à la qualité de service des applications métiers. Missions Principales Assurer le suivi quotidien de la production IBM i (AS400). Superviser et contrôler les traitements batch, en veillant à leur bon déroulement. Analyser, diagnostiquer et résoudre les incidents de production. Gérer les relances, les reprises et les corrections des traitements en erreur. Assurer le suivi et l’exploitation des flux de données via les solutions MFT. Superviser les opérations de sauvegarde et de restauration. Participer aux mises en production et aux opérations techniques associées. Assurer la mise à jour des procédures et de la documentation d’exploitation. Participer aux cellules de crise en cas d’incident majeur. Contribuer à l’amélioration continue des processus et des pratiques d’exploitation. Les missions énumérées ne sont pas exhaustives, il s'agit des missions principales. Profil Vous justifiez de plus de 5 ans d’expérience en exploitation informatique, idéalement dans des environnements de production critiques. Vous maîtrisez IBM i (AS400) et possédez une bonne connaissance des outils BRMS, Robot400, GoAnywhere MFT et MIMIX. Vous avez une solide expérience du suivi de production, de l’exploitation des traitements batch, de la gestion des incidents et des flux MFT. Vous êtes rigoureux, réactif et autonome, et êtes disponible pour assurer des astreintes (1 semaine sur 4) ainsi que des interventions ponctuelles en heures non ouvrées. Seront appréciées : une expérience dans le secteur bancaire, la connaissance des bonnes pratiques ITIL et des dispositifs de sauvegarde et de reprise d’activité (PRA/PCA).
